statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-11586: curl answers every WebSocket PING automatically with no upper bound on memory held for unacknowledged frames, so a malicious server can exhaust the client's memory by flooding it with PINGs. curl 8.16.0 to 8.20.0 are affected; 8.21.0 is not (also 8.16.1 and 8.20.1 on older branches): https://curl.se/docs/CVE-2026-11586.html. The fix, https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/849317ff5c5a5e13f50ec3d001e46ddffa77d8a4, is in the curl-8_21_0 release tag and not in curl-8_20_0. This owner's Alpine 3.23 builds are 8.17.0-r1, 8.18.0-r0, 8.19.0-r0, 8.20.0-r0, 8.20.0-r1, 8.21.0-r0, 8.22.0-r0, 8.23.0-r0 and 8.23.0-r1. On x86_64 and aarch64, the libcurl library and the curl program in each report the curl release of the package version. Builds 8.17.0-r1 to 8.20.0-r1 package curl 8.17.0 to 8.20.0 without the fix (8.20.0-r1 is a rebuild of curl 8.20.0 that adds no patch) and are affected; 8.21.0-r0 and later package curl 8.21.0 or newer, which contain it. Alpine's 3.23-stable curl APKBUILD lists this CVE under its 8.22.0-r0 secfixes (https://gitlab.alpinelinux.org/alpine/aports/-/blob/3.23-stable/main/curl/APKBUILD); this owner's own 8.21.0-r0 build already ships the fixed upstream release. The range ends at 8.21.0-r0.
